items.title: Bob Lovett Interview, 1949-04-01
items.q: No, I think I was mainly trying to emulate the sound of Johnny Dodds.

ctx.x: G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Was there an effort to emulate his tone and effects as well as just the phrase?
G-E-R-O-U-L-D. No, I think I was mainly trying to emulate the sound of Johnny Dodds.

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Even that early or after the Dodds? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. I think so, yes. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Because? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Because to me it seemed like a good, strong, gutsy sort of thing. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. As you recall, I mentioned that later in a chapter in New Perspectives of Jazz, where your playing in the Dodds style had impressed me so that years later I remembered it. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. How did you have to come to Chicago?
